lonely: WRITE FROM THE PUSHED-ASIDE VIEWER'S SIDE
Before you write, picture one real person who was told 'not now' today. Write so that person feels seen in the first two seconds and is not pushed aside by the last line.
depth: Mine Mark 10:13-16 for the details most people skip (who brought the children, what they asked for, who stopped them, the one place Mark says Jesus was 'much displeased', what His hands did). Build the film on the richest detail you find.
hook: Most viewers decide in 2 seconds. Write the strongest honest hook you can and make every line pull to the next. The payoff must be worth the wait.
plain: Write so a viewer with school English and no Bible knowledge understands every line on first hearing, and a lifelong Bible reader still learns something.
judge: Write the best film you can. Use your own judgment on everything.
